solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Make sense in total

definitions.meaning: an argument that makes sense is one whose parts fit together and convince
to total figures is to sum them into one number

explanation.definitionFit: Both are idiomatic senses of one phrasal verb: a story that is coherent does this, and so does an accountant summing a column.

clue.text: A sailor looking up guide to the world

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman consults a book of charts to find his way about the world.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of maps is the standard reference guide to the countries of the globe.

clue.text: In which spare food is taken back to the lab?

definitions.text: In which spare food is taken back to the lab?

parts.words: In which spare food is taken back to the lab?
parts.note: the 'lab' is not a laboratory but a Labrador, the family pet for whom restaurant leftovers are supposedly packed

explanation.walkthrough: 'lab' suggests a scientist taking leftovers to work; it is short for Labrador, the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Diners ask for this container to carry restaurant leftovers home, nominally for the household pet.

clue.text: Nature god initially defending a creature that's endangered

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild, shepherds and nature

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the word defending is used

explanation.surface: A woodland deity stands guard over an animal at risk of dying out.
explanation.definitionFit: The black-and-white bamboo-eating bear of China is a famous example of a threatened species.

clue.text: Officer's fabric more important to clothe worker

indicators.note: to clothe something is to wrap it round, so the outer pieces enclose the worker

parts.note: serge is a hard-wearing twilled cloth, often used for uniforms
major means greater or more significant
the worker is the worker ant of crossword convention

explanation.surface: A senior officer's cloth is deemed too important to waste on dressing a mere labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to clothe' wraps the fabric and the more-important word round the worker. The 's after Officer is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the senior non-commissioned rank in a battalion, the drill-shouting warrant officer of army life.

clue.text: Criminal's nice house and home

parts.note: a villa is a large, attractive country or seaside house
if you are at home you are in

explanation.surface: A crook's luxurious residence serves as his base.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Criminal is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer or scoundrel, the bad character of a story or the dock, is a synonym for a lawbreaker.

clue.text: Cereal-producing palm, small in the past

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
ago means earlier, in the past

explanation.surface: A tree that yields grain was once only a little one.
explanation.definitionFit: The starchy granules used in milk puddings come from the pith of a tropical palm of that name.

clue.text: Beef beats fish

parts.note: to top a rival is to beat or outdo them
the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Meat comes out ahead of seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef' looks like a complaint or a verb; it is the cut of meat, TOPSIDE being a lean joint from the top of the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a lean cut from the upper hind leg of the cow, a classic roasting joint.

clue.text: Coffee's nice aroma wafting about

indicators.note: smells wafting about drift and swirl, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A cup of black coffee gives off a pleasant smell that drifts round the room.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Coffee is read as 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an espresso diluted with hot water, a standard order in any café.

clue.text: Connect to computer using identifying symbol and name

parts.note: a logo is the emblem that identifies a company or brand

explanation.surface: Accessing a system requires a recognisable icon and your user name.
explanation.definitionFit: To start a session on a computer system, entering your credentials, is the phrasal verb wanted.

clue.text: Gibbet shines, fitted with aluminium

indicators.note: fitted with means the word for shines has the metal installed inside it

parts.note: something that glows shines with light
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A hanging post gleams because it has been fitted with shiny metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A gibbet is a gallows-like upright with an arm from which executed bodies were hung, so the words are near synonyms.

clue.text: Malicious programs such as Bond might use?

definitions.meaning: software that covertly gathers information from a computer
read as two words, the equipment or goods an agent like James Bond would carry

explanation.surface: Harmful software is the sort of kit James Bond would deploy.
explanation.definitionFit: Programs that secretly monitor a user and send data away are a familiar class of malware.

clue.text: A requirement to mask one's strong scent

indicators.note: to mask is to cover over, so the requirement wraps round the other piece

parts.note: a need is something required
one's is read as I'S, I for one plus 'S, giving the letters for 'is'

explanation.surface: Something with a powerful smell is needed to hide another odour.
explanation.definitionFit: The seed of anise has a pungent liquorice smell, so it serves as an example of a strong aroma.

clue.text: Mischievous adventure has disturbed peace — sad

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A prank has left the calm upset and someone unhappy.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild or reckless exploit, often embarrassing afterwards, is the standard meaning of the word.

clue.text: Nothing at first? Points out choices

indicators.note: at first means the nothing letter goes at the very front

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of Points are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether there is nothing to start with, and is shown the alternatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Alternatives you may select from are synonyms of the plural noun used here.

clue.text: Sort of car for 5? I don't believe it!

definitions.meaning: the criminal at 5-down flees a robbery in the vehicle waiting outside
an exclamation of disbelief, as in British 'you're kidding'

explanation.definitionFit: The escape vehicle of a heist and the incredulous exclamation 'go on!' share one phrase.

clue.text: Dye farmworkers applied to tail of beast

parts.note: pigmen are farm labourers who tend the pigs

indicators.note: tail of means the final letter of the word beast

explanation.surface: Farmhands put colouring on an animal's tail, perhaps to mark it.
explanation.definitionFit: A colouring substance, such as is used to tint paint or fabric, is a close synonym of a dye.

clue.text: So keen a Colonel?

definitions.meaning: the idiom 'keen as' this condiment means very enthusiastic
Colonel of that name is a suspect in the board game Cluedo (Clue in North America)

explanation.definitionFit: The yellow condiment appears in the idiom of eagerness and names a Cluedo suspect.

clue.text: Note, part of lush arpeggio

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A musical tone forms one piece of a rich broken chord.
explanation.definitionFit: A tone raised by a semitone, such as F-sharp, is called by this name in music.

clue.text: Mummy's rhyme that soothes baby

parts.note: the word wanted rhymes with mummy and is the rubber teat a mother gives an infant to suck

explanation.walkthrough: 'rhyme' suggests a nursery rhyme; it means a word rhyming with Mummy.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English a baby's pacifier, the rubber teat given to calm it, has this name.

clue.text: State has popular princess

parts.note: something that is in is fashionable or popular
Diana, Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: A country boasts a well-loved royal.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the fifty US states, in the Midwest, with Indianapolis as capital.

clue.text: Begin to appear, waving wand

indicators.note: a wand being waved moves about, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A magician waves a wand and something starts to materialise.
explanation.definitionFit: When an idea starts to become clear, or the day breaks, it is said to emerge in this way.

clue.text: Frightening sort of clock

definitions.meaning: read as a noun, the act of frightening, a sudden fear or scare
a clock that rings to wake you at a set time

explanation.definitionFit: The word means sudden fear and also names the bedside clock that rings in the morning.

clue.text: Fresh effort for millennial government

parts.note: fresh means new
labour is hard work or effort

explanation.surface: A renewed push by the administration at the turn of the century.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Blair's rebranded Labour Party governed Britain from 1997, so it ran the country at the turn of the millennium.

clue.text: Shame about end of true religious devotion

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for shame goes round the other letter

parts.note: as in 'what a shame', a pity

indicators.note: end of means only the final letter of true is used

explanation.surface: It is a pity that sincere faith comes to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: Devoutness, reverence for God and religious duty, is what the word means.
